claims.label: Theorem 1 (K2, c=1) — unconditional
claims.claim: h_K2(n) = n for all n >= 1 (every K2-free graph is edgeless, alpha = n; and the edgeless graph is K2-free, so the min is attained at hom = n). Table n=1..7: 1,2,3,4,5,6,7.

claims.label: Theorem 2 (P3 classification + sharp law) — unconditional
claims.claim: P3-free <=> disjoint union of cliques (both directions). Hence h_P3(n) = ceil(sqrt(n)) EXACTLY (hom >= ceil(sqrt(n)) by max(largest clique, number of parts); witness = balanced disjoint union of cliques). Table n=1..7: 1,2,2,2,3,3,3. Exponent c(P3)=1/2.

claims.label: Theorem 3 (3K1 complement-side law with the C5 honesty correction) — unconditional
claims.claim: h_3K1(n) >= t_n := min{t : t(t+1) >= n} = ceil((sqrt(4n+1)-1)/2), with equality at n in {1,3,4,5,7} and strictness at n in {2,6} (Ramsey forcing R(3,3)=6). HONESTY: the naive real-valued claim hom >= sqrt(n) is FALSE — C5 is 3K1-free on n=5 with hom(C5)=2 < sqrt(5). Table n=1..7: 1,2,2,2,2,3,3.

claims.label: Theorem 4 (substitution closure, uniform blow-up frame) — unconditional in-frame
claims.claim: For uniform blow-ups G of quotient Q on q vertices with classes X_i of size s: (1) if Q is H1-free then hom(G) >= hom(Q); (2) if Q is not H1-free then some class is H2-free (when G is H1[H2]-free); (3) hom(G) >= min(h_H1(q), h_H2(s)); (4) balanced exponents give f(c1,c2) = c1c2/(c1+c2); (5) multi-level harmonic law F_k = (sum_i 1/c_i)^{-1} — exact rational identities: f(1/2,1/2)=1/4, 3-level (1/2,1/2,1/2) -> 1/6, (1/2,1/3,2/3) -> 2/13. General-graph closure attributed to Alon-Pach-Solymosi (honest scope). Identities: K2[K2] ≅ K4; 2K1[K2] ≅ 2K2; K2[2K1] ≅ C4; complement(P3[K2]) ≅ C4 ∪ 2K1.

claims.label: Theorem 5 (baseline certificate) — cited
claims.claim: exp(c_H sqrt(log n)) baseline for induced-H-free graphs (Erdos-Hajnal 1977) — cited, not comparator-certified beyond the context block.

claims.label: The F7 family theorem (kernel W68-61K scope) — unconditional
claims.claim: For F7 = {K1, K2, Kbar2, P3, Pbar3, K3, Kbar3}: every H-free graph on n vertices contains a clique OR an independent set of size >= floor(sqrt(n)) (SHARP; c(H)=1/2). Tightness witness: for every j >= 1, the disjoint union of 2^j copies of K_{2^j} (n = 4^j vertices) has max(omega,alpha) = 2^j = floor(sqrt(n)) EXACTLY. The eighth mission member P4 (Seinsche) is the continuation front — NOT claimed.
